messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert — p95 latency regression observed on /v1/generate. auto-pager -> @Maya (oncall). detectors: serving-runtime latency anomaly, slight uptick in 5xxs :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): ack. jumping in. Any recent deploys?
Maya (oncall): paging secondary oncall if needed.
deploy-bot: finished deploy 1748009800 by ci/cd — image=redwood/runtime:v2.19, change=kernel-tuning + batching heuristic update. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/9843 :hammer:
Samir SRE: I'm on. us-west-2 showing strongest regression. p95 baseline ~180ms -> current ~1.6s.
Olivia (PM): CS reports two customers seeing timeouts on generate endpoints. Marking impact as customer-visible.
Maya (oncall): quick health checks: health endpoints green, but /v1/generate latency high. local curl check: `curl -s -w "%{time_total}" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood/v1/generate` -> 1.48
Jules (runtime): pulling runtime logs. I'm seeing worker threads stuck on blocking ops in tail logs.
Jules (runtime): logs paste:
```
2026-06-03T11:59:58Z worker-12 request_id=abc123 duration_ms=1520 model=gpt-like context_tokens=512
2026-06-03T12:00:00Z worker-7 request_id=def456 duration_ms=1480 model=gpt-like context_tokens=256
2026-06-03T12:00:02Z worker-12 request_id=ghi789 duration_ms=1700 model=gpt-like context_tokens=1024
```
Maya (oncall): running `kubectl top pods` in us-west-2 — CPU and memory look normal, no OOMs.
Samir SRE: kernel logs from node-42 show watchdog/blocking around the deploy window:
```
[Jun  3 11:58:44] watchdog: tasks blocked for more than 120 seconds.
[Jun  3 11:58:44]  "kworker/3:2" cpu:2 state: D stack: 0x00000000
```
Samir SRE: suggests kernel-level blocking rather than application OOM.
Ravi (oncall-2): taking handoff from Maya. I'll own live mitigation while Maya builds timeline.
Maya (oncall): handing off. Mitigation options: 1) revert runtime:v2.19 2) shift traffic to fallback pool (v2.18) 3) restart affected worker pods.
Ravi (oncall-2): applying temporary routing: `rbctl route set-rule /v1/generate fallback_pool=10% --until=+15m` to divert some traffic.
incident-bot: routing rule applied by Ravi at 1748010200.
Ravi (oncall-2): after 10% diversion, p95 reduced from 1.6s -> 620ms. Increasing route to 40% to test effect.
Ravi (oncall-2): after moving 40% of traffic, p95 ~320ms, p50 ~260ms. Error rate dropping.
Jules (runtime): grabbed a slow trace (trace id: tr-9b2c). Span breakdown:
```
span: request_total 1500ms
  span: model_decode 22ms
  span: kv_cache_lookup 800ms   <-- large
  span: batch_queue_wait 600ms
  span: kernel_wait epoll_wait 78ms
```
Jules (runtime): kv_cache_lookup and batch_queue_wait dominate total time. Investigating whether kv lookups are remote-blocking.
Samir SRE: perf counters on node-42: `perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-clock,cycles,instructions` for 30s showed context-switches ~1.1M vs baseline ~80k. `vmstat` confirms high cs value; swap activity minimal.
Samir SRE: early hypotheses: A) batching heuristic in v2.19 increases queueing for large-context requests causing head-of-line waits; B) kernel scheduling interactions cause long kernel blocking under this workload; C) multi-key KV lookups elevated latency under larger batches.
Maya (oncall): timeline so far:
- 11:50 local baseline p95 ~180ms
- 11:57 deploy runtime:v2.19 started (deploy-bot)
- 11:58 first kernel watchdog messages on node-42
- 12:00 p95 spikes to ~1.6s, customers report timeouts
- 12:05 routing fallback (10%) applied by Ravi -> p95 ~620ms
- 12:10 routing increased to 40% -> p95 ~320ms
- 12:25 rolling restarts and further mitigations applied
Olivia (PM): please send mitigation summary and ETA to CS. We need customer communication.
Jules (runtime): correlating logs by request size: requests with context_tokens >=512 hit slow path more often. Kv cache multi-get miss rate increases with size. Batching seems to amplify multi-key KV load.
Ravi (oncall-2): performed rolling restart of runtime workers on node-42 to clear potential kernel stuck tasks: `kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime-worker -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-42` executed.
incident-bot: restart command executed at 1748010400.
Ravi (oncall-2): post-restart p95 improved to ~240ms. Stability holding.
Samir SRE: saved perf data and bpftrace snapshots to internal artifact store for offline analysis. Short bpftrace probe caught spikes on `runtime-worker` in `sys_enter_poll`.
Jules (runtime): batcher metrics show wait_time tail elevated. Kernel trace suggests `ksoftirqd` and kworker preemption spikes. I'll add instrumentation: chunk KV multi-get into smaller batches, add timeouts on KV lookup, and cap batch sizes for very large contexts as experiment.
Maya (oncall): documenting hypotheses inline:
- H1: batching heuristic change in v2.19 increases head-of-line blocking on large-context requests -> p95 regression.
- H2: kernel scheduling/epoll interaction under new runtime paths exposes long-blocking kernel tasks.
- H3: remote KV multi-get latency spikes when batched heavily, causing blocked workers.
Samir SRE: early evidence: perf/context-switch metrics and kernel watchdog match H2; remote KV traces show occasional 500-800ms responses on multi-key lookups, supporting H3; batching metrics from runtime support H1. Likely multi-factor.
Olivia (PM): capture list of affected customer request ids, mitigation steps, and impact window for CS.
Maya (oncall): sample affected request ids captured: [abc123, def456, ghi789]. Sending to CS. Assigning RCA owners: Jules for runtime/batching, Samir for node/kernel analysis, Maya to draft incident report.
Jules (runtime): next steps: implement size-based batching cap, chunked KV multi-get, and fail-fast timeout on KV. Plan to run these as canary patch after RCA validation.
Samir SRE: infra tasks: enumerate kernel versions across cluster, check for recent kernel updates, reproduce with synthetic workload hitting KV multi-get under batching, and correlate with perf snapshots.
Maya (oncall): live status: traffic gradually shifted back; p95 stable ~250ms in us-west-2. Marking incident mitigated. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-517.
Olivia (PM): scheduling RCA deep-dive tomorrow 09:00 PT. Owners confirmed: Jules (runtime), Samir (infra), Maya (writeup).
Ravi (oncall-2): note for playbook — if similar regression after runtime change, immediate rollback to v2.18 should be primary mitigation.
Maya (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll compile timeline, attach logs/traces, and move conversation to RCA channel for follow-up. Closing live thread. :thumbsup:
